rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command follows the people's denial in 6:66; the switch to a relative clause singles out the especially abusive subset who attack the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: عطف على جملة { وكذب به قومك } ( الأنعام : 66 ) . والعدول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most deniers rejected without polemic, but the fiercest group publicly attacked the Qur'an; the Prophet must leave their debate and gatherings until they stop, since shunning all deniers would halt preaching.
rows.anchor: فأولئك قسم ، والذين يخوضون في الآيات قسم كان أبذى وأقذع ، وأشد كفرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing them means seeing them while they are actively engaged in their polemics.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { إذا رأيت الذين يخوضون } إذا رأيتهم في حال خوضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative construction, rather than a bare label or pronoun, explains the unusual withdrawal order: their conduct supplies its rationale and withdrawal lasts until they do its opposite.
rows.anchor: لأن الموصول فيه إيماء إلى وجه الأمر بالإعراض لأنه أمر غريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is an exemplary case of a relative clause hinting at the cause of an ensuing report or command; its endpoint is the end of the conduct in the clause.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية أحسن ما يمثل به ، لمجيء الموصول للإيماء إلى إفادة تعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur says the verse supports al-Qutb al-Shirazi's reading of al-Sakkaki: the basis of a statement is its cause; al-Taftazani rejected that interpretation.
rows.anchor: صحة ما فسر به القطب الشيرازي في ( شرح المفتاح ) قول السكاكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawd literally means entering water on foot rather than swimming, then metaphorically denotes burdensome or difficult action and contrived talk.
rows.anchor: والخوض حقيقته الدخول في الماء مشيا بالرجلين دون سباحة ثم استعير

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says Qur'anic usage of khawd is mostly blameworthy initiation; here it means speaking falsely and mockingly about God's signs.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : وأكثر ما ورد في القرآن ورد فيما يذم الشروع فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding the case of forgetfulness further emphasizes the order to withdraw from the mockers.
rows.anchor: عطف حالة النسيان زيادة في تأكيد الأمر بالإعراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ascribing forgetfulness to Satan indicates that human constitution gives Satan a share in some natural symptoms; this is not Satan whispering into the Prophet's actions, from which he is protected.
rows.anchor: فدلنا على أن النسيان من آثار الخلقة التي جعل الله فيها حظا العلم الشيطان

rows.speaker: جمهور علماء السنة من الأشاعرة وغيرهم
rows.claim: The Sunni majority, including Ash'aris, allow prophets to forget in matters other than conveying revelation; Ibn al-Arabi says major Rafidites deny prophetic forgetfulness, and a view is also attributed to some Ash'aris and Abu Ishaq al-Isfarayini.
rows.anchor: فالنسيان من الأعراض البشرية الجائزة على الأنبياء في غير تبليغ ما أمروا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Reports say the Prophet once ended a four-rak'ah prayer after two rak'ahs and forgot verses until another man's night recitation reminded him; the source calls these reports authentic.
rows.anchor: وقد نسي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فسلم من ركعتين في الصلاة الرباعية

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that he is human and forgets as his followers do, so they should remind him when he forgets; Ibn Ashur calls the hadith authentic.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح : ( إنما أنا بشر أنسى كما تنسون فإذا نسيت فذكروني )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The issue is not whether forgetfulness can occur, but how it can be attributed to Satan: God may make some permissible bodily symptoms, like yawning or pleurisy, effects of Satan, while others are assigned to angels.
rows.anchor: وليس نظرنا في جواز ذلك وإنما نظرنا في إسناد ذلك إلى الشيطان

rows.speaker: أيوب عليه السلام
rows.claim: Job said that Satan had afflicted him with distress and torment, an example of a bodily trial attributed to Satan.
rows.anchor: وقد قال أيوب { أني مسني الشيطان بنصب وعذاب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permissible human symptoms that neither compromise transmission nor cause sin may be effects of Satan; God protects prophets from Satan in other respects.
rows.anchor: الأعراض البشرية الجائزة على الأنبياء التي لا تخل بتبليغ ولا توقع في المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible view is that Muhammad alone was protected from every satanic influence, even one causing otherwise permissible human symptoms.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم قد خص من بين الأنبياء بأن لا سلطة

rows.speaker: جبريل
rows.claim: In the chest-splitting report, Gabriel called what he removed the Prophet's share of Satan, understood as the center of Satan's influence.
rows.anchor: أن جبريل لما استخرج العلقة قال : هذا حظ الشيطان منك

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the Muwatta report, the Prophet left Bilal to watch for dawn; Satan kept soothing Bilal like a child until he slept and sunrise came.
rows.anchor: حين نام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ووكل بلالا بأن يكلأ لهم الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this account, the Prophet and the other Muslims slept naturally; only Bilal's sleep was caused by Satan.
rows.anchor: فأما نوم النبي والمسلمين عدا بلالا فكان نوما معتادا ليس من عمل الشيطان

rows.speaker: عياض
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur says this account is indicated by Qadi Iyad in al-Shifa.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا الوجه أشار عياض في ( الشفاء )

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet saw the Night of Decree and went to tell people, but two men quarreled and it was lifted; Satan caused their quarrel because he could not lift the night himself.
rows.anchor: رأى ليلة القدر ، فخرج ليعلم الناس فتلاحى رجلان فرفعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is protected from Satanic whispering, but need not be protected from lower effects such as forgetfulness or distraction; whispering produces positive effects while forgetfulness and distraction produce absences.
rows.anchor: الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم معصوم من الوسوسة ، وأما ما دونها مثل الإنساء والنزغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Satan makes the Prophet forget to withdraw, the command means that once he remembers, he must leave; this forgetfulness redirects him between forms of worship or preaching without sin or Satan achieving misguidance.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى إن أنساك الشيطان الإعراض عنهم فإن تذكرت فلا تقعد معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has lifted accountability for forgetfulness, and the prohibition applies after the Prophet recalls the order to withdraw.
rows.anchor: وقد رفع الله المؤاخذة بالنسيان ، ولذلك قال : { فلا تقعد بعد الذكرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dhikra is a noun meaning recollection, opposite of forgetfulness; the clause describes remembering after an inadvertent lapse and sitting with the mockers.
rows.anchor: فالذكرى اسم للتذكر وهو ضد النسيان ، فهي اسم مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to do something entails forbidding its opposite; leaving the gathering after remembrance is the opposite of withdrawing from it.
rows.anchor: وهو ضد فأعرض ، وذلك أن الأمر بالشيء نهي عن ضده

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read yunsiyannaka with a vowelless n and an ungeminated s.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور : { ينسينك } بسكون النون وتخفيف السين

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Amir reads the form with an opened n and geminated s, from the intensive verb tansi'a.
rows.anchor: وقرأه ابن عامر بفتح النون وتشديد السين من التنسية

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars interpret the address to the Prophet as intended for his community, as in the warning about shirk in 39:65.
rows.anchor: ومن العلماء من تأول هذه الآية بأنها مما خوطب به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد أمته

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says there is no excuse for applying the community-address interpretation here: unlike shirk in 39:65, forgetfulness is possible for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن العربي إذا عذرنا أصحابنا في قولهم ذلك في { لئن أشركت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are the people who polemicize about God's signs; naming them explicitly in place of a pronoun stresses that their polemic is wrongdoing and stubborn denial of truth.
rows.anchor: والقوم الظالمون هم الذين يخوضون في آيات الله ، فهذا من الإظهار في مقام الإضمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage shifts from earlier proofs of oneness, resurrection, and messengership to visible wonders of creation, proving God's sole divinity and disproving Arab idolatry, and a fortiori materialist denial.
rows.anchor: استئناف ابتدائي انتقل به من تقرير التوحيد والبعث والرسالة وأفانين المواعظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address reproaches the polytheists for ingratitude, while giving believers knowledge, certainty, deeper knowledge of their Lord, and greater gratitude.
rows.anchor: وفيه علم ويقين للمؤمنين من المصدقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although no one denies that God performs these acts, the subtle inference from plant growth to resurrection was neglected; the polytheists' denial makes their state like doubt, warranting emphasis with inna.
rows.anchor: كان حالهم كحال من أنكر أو شك في أن الله فالق الحب والنوى ، فأكد الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal sentence marks this description as enduring and essential to God; it is an attribute of action or of power and its relations in the terminology of those who deny action-attributes.
rows.anchor: وجيء بالجملة الاسمية للدلالة على ثبات هذا الوصف دوامه لأنه وصف ذاتي لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence does not express exclusivity, because its immediate purpose is to show God's power to bring life from death, not to make a restrictive assertion.
rows.anchor: لم يؤت في هذا الخبر بما يقتضي الحصر إذ ليس المقام مقام القصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falaq is splitting or cleaving parts apart; here it is the cleft from which shoots and roots of plants and trees emerge, displaying divine knowledge, power, and wisdom.
rows.anchor: والفلق : شق وصدع بعض أجزاء الشيء عن بعض ، والمقصود الفلق الذي تنبثق منه وشائج النبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-habb is a collective noun for what plants yield, singular habba; al-nawa is a collective noun for fruit stones, singular nawa, including date and other fruit kernels from which trees grow.
rows.anchor: والحب اسم جمع لما يثمره النبت ، واحده حبة . والنوى اسم جمع نواة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is a second predicate of inna, explaining the seed-splitting as living plant growth from lifeless hard seed, while its broader meaning also includes animals emerging from sperm or eggs.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { يخرج الحي من الميت } في محل خبر ثان عن اسم ( إن )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur favors separating the clause without a conjunction: it clarifies the first predicate, or can be a separate broader predicate clarifying it; conjunction is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: فلذلك رجح فصل هذه الجملة عن التي قبلها إلا أنها أعم منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing dead from living is the opposite wonder, displaying complete divine power and denying nature's capacity to create; a freely acting agent produces opposites, unlike a natural cause.
rows.anchor: لأنه إخبار بضد مضمون { يخرج الحي من الميت } وصنع آخر عجيب دال على كمال القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause elaborates seed-splitting: plants yield lifeless dried grain and fruits hold lifeless stones; living animals also yield eggs, milk, musk, pearls, and bezoar stones.
rows.anchor: منها حال إثمار النبات والشجر : حبا ييبس وهو في قصب نباته فلا تكون فيه حياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers connecting this clause to the preceding life-from-death clause as its completion, like the paired clauses about dawn and night in 6:96.
rows.anchor: وقد رجح عطف هذا الخبر لأنه كالتكملة لقوله : { يخرج الحي من الميت

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari instead connects the clause to faliq al-habb, since splitting grain produces life from death, not dead from living; Ibn Ashur says the alternative connection is less apparent.
rows.anchor: وجعله في ( الكشاف ) عطفا على { فالق الحب } بناء على أن مضمون قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verbal clause presents bringing life from death as deliberate, known action that recurs continually rather than coincidence.
rows.anchor: وقد جيء بجملة : { يخرج الحي من الميت } فعلية للدلالة على أن هذا الفعل يتجدد ويتكرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The participial clause conveys permanence; together, the two forms make both processes recurring and constant, numerous and intrinsic, with neither process privileged.
rows.anchor: وجيء في قوله : { ومخرج الميت من الحي } اسما للدلالة على الدوام والثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative sharply identifies the agent of these immense acts, while hinting at the addressees' obtuseness; only this God known by his great name is divine, so the following question results.
rows.anchor: والإشارة ب { ذلكم } لزيادة التمييز وللتعريض بغباوة المخاطبين المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afk is turning someone away from a place or action; here it asks how the people are turned away from God's oneness.
rows.anchor: والأفك بفتح الهمزة مصدر أفكه يأفكه ، من باب ضرب ، إذا صرفه عن مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anna means from where; the question expresses incredulous rejection, since nothing could rightly turn them away from God's oneness.
rows.anchor: و ( أنى ) بمعنى من أين . وهو استفهام تعجيبي إنكاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is passive because no single cause of their turning is identifiable: Satan's whispering, leaders' misguidance, and their own desires combine.
rows.anchor: وبني فعل { تؤفكون } للمجهول لعدم تعين صارفهم عن توحيد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That is Allah is an independent sentence for reflection, making the ensuing how-are-you-turned-away clause parenthetical.
rows.anchor: وجملة ( ذلكم الله ) مستأنفة مقصود منها الاعتبار ، فتكون جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faliq al-isbah may be a fourth predicate of inna or an adjective of Allah in the demonstrative clause, leaving the turning-away question parenthetical.
rows.anchor: { فالق الإصباح } يجوز أن يكون خبرا رابعا عن اسم ( إن ) ، ويجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-isbah originally names the horizon becoming morning, then the dawn itself: the light of daybreak, opposed to night.
rows.anchor: والإصباح بكسر الهمزة في الأصل مصدر أصبح الأفق ، إذا صار ذا صباح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dawn's appearance is metaphorically pictured as splitting darkness, as in the verse about stripping day from night.
rows.anchor: فلق الإصباح استعارة لظهور الضياء في ظلمة الليل ، فشبه ذلك بفلق الظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive is treated as genuine by the participle's noun-like quality, though its verbal quality also permits a construct; since it describes a past act, its resemblance to an active present participle is weak.
rows.anchor: لأن اسم الفاعل له شائبة الاسمية فيضاف إضافة حقيقية ، وله شائبة فعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, dawn can be construed as what is split from, with the preposition omitted; night is what is actually cleft, so commentators explain it as splitting the darkness before daybreak, a striking display of power and a boon for life and work.
rows.anchor: أي فالق عن الإصباح فانتصب على نزع الخافض ، ولذلك سموا الصبح فلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about making night a repose is coordinated with the clause about splitting dawn.
rows.anchor: { وجاعل الليل سكنا } عطف على { فالق الإصباح }

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read ja'il as an active participle and al-layl in the genitive.
rows.anchor: وقرأه الجمهور بصيغة اسم الفاعل وجر { الليل }

rows.speaker: عاصم ، وحمزة ، والكسائي ، وخلف
rows.claim: Asim, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read ja'ala as a past verb and al-layl in the accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأه عاصم ، وحمزة ، والكسائي ، وخلف . { وجعل } بصيغة فعل الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since darkness is absence, God's act here is removing the light that prevents darkness; he apportions the light rather than leaving it constant, so creatures can rest after labor.
rows.anchor: وعبر في جانب الليل بمادة الجعل لأن الظلمة عدم فتعلق القدرة فيها هو تعلقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sakan denotes what one rests in, a metaphorical repose of the soul and reassurance of the heart; here night brings rest from work.
rows.anchor: أي تسكن إليه النفس ويطمئن إليه القلب ، والسكون فيه مجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wives and houses are also called sakan, as in 16:80, because people find repose in them.
rows.anchor: وتسمى الزوجة سكنا والبيت سكنا قال تعالى : { والله جعل لكم من بيوتكم سكنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sun and moon are accusative by coordination to the syntactic position of al-layl, which functions as the object despite its genitive form; Arabic permits coordination by syntactic case.
rows.anchor: وعطف { الشمس والقمر } على { الليل } بالنصب رعيا لمحل الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hisaban is a verbal noun like ghufran, shukran, and kufran: the sun and moon serve as measures for time, day and night, months, seasons, and years.
rows.anchor: والحسبان في الأصل مصدر حسب بفتح السين كالغفران ، والشكران ، والكفران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many peoples reckon months and years by the sun's passage through the zodiac, while Arabs reckon by lunar stations and Islam uses the lunar calendar; pre-Islamic intercalation aligned years with seasons.
rows.anchor: لأن كثيرا من الأمم يحسبون شهورهم وأعوامهم بحساب سير الشمس بحلولها في البروج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stable, ordered motions of both bodies benefit people beyond religious calendrics and demonstrate divine knowledge and power; deeper knowledge of their system would make the sign still greater.
rows.anchor: وإنما استقام ذلك للناس بجعل الله حركات الشمس والقمر على نظام واحد لا يختلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is linked to the preceding mention of making night a repose; it recalls divine oneness, the stars' wondrous creation, and their benefit as guides on land and sea.
rows.anchor: عطف على جملة : { وجاعل الليل سكنا } ( الأنعام : 96 ) ، وهذا تذكير بوحدانية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mapping of stellar motions and risings and settings was among humanity's oldest sciences, appearing among Chaldeans and ancient Egyptians and guiding the development of astronomy.
rows.anchor: وقد كان ضبط حركات النجوم ومطالعها ومغاربها من أقدم العلوم البشرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The main aim is to prove God's unique divinity; defining both subject and predicate makes the clause restrictive, though the audience already acknowledged God's creation of stars and their usefulness.
rows.anchor: فلذلك صيغ بصيغة القصر بطريق تعريف المسند والمسند إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stars are the celestial bodies that shine in the night sky and appear small to the eye; the moon is not a star.
rows.anchor: والنجوم جمع نجم ، وهو الكوكب ، أي الجسم الكروي المضيء في الأفق ليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ja'ala means created and takes one object; lakum attaches to it, addresses all humanity, and its lām expresses purpose.
rows.anchor: و { جعل } هنا بمعنى خلق ، فيتعدى إلى مفعول واحد و { لكم } . متعلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance clause is a second purpose of creation; the first lām expresses benefaction, while the second gives the wisdom and benefit, and guidance is nearly an explicative substitute with its governing verb repeated.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { لتهتدوا بها } علة ثانية ل { جعل } فاللام للعلة أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Darknesses means intense darkness; Arabic commonly uses the plural rather than the singular for this sense, as in the earlier verse about people left in darknesses.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالظلمات : الظلمة الشديدة ، فصيغة الجمع مستعملة في القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The annexation can mean darknesses occurring in land and sea; those rejecting an in-meaning take it as a lām-relation of slight association, like the expression planet of the awkward woman.
rows.anchor: وإضافة ظلمات } إلى { البر والبحر } على معنى ( في ) لأن الظلمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent account in al-Miftah treats slight-association annexation as a similarity-based metaphor, like the earth swallowing its water in 11:44.
rows.anchor: فهو استعارة على ما هو ظاهر كلام ( المفتاح ) في مبحث البلاغة والفصاحة

rows.speaker: التفتزاني
rows.claim: Al-Taftazani calls slight-association annexation a figurative attribution, since literal lām-annexation expresses complete relation or ownership.
rows.anchor: إذ قال في ( كوكب الخرقاء ) ( حقيقة الإضافة اللامية الاختصاص الكامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur suggests al-Taftazani may distinguish the figures by how closely the slight association approaches ownership; the phrase itself suggests figurative attribution.
rows.anchor: ولعل التفتزاني يرى الاختلاف في المجاز باختلاف قرب الإضافة لأدنى ملابسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The independent sentence records and delivers the signs to remove excuses from unbelievers; its lām makes the detailed signs serve those who know.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { قد فصلنا الآيات } مستأنفة للتسجيل والتبليغ وقطع معذرة من لم يؤمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The detailing of signs was discussed earlier in the sura at 6:55.
rows.anchor: وتفصيل الآيات تقدم عند قوله تعالى : { وكذلك نفصل الآيات في هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article is comprehensive, covering the sign of creating stars and all other signs.
rows.anchor: والتعريف في الآيات } للاستغراق فيشمل آية خلق النجوم وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge in Arabic is apprehending things as they are; two cited poets contrast the knowledgeable person with the ignorant.
rows.anchor: والعلم في كلام العرب إدراك الأشياء على ما هي عليه قال السموأل أو عبد الملك الحارثي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who know are people who benefit from the signs and believe in God alone, as stated at 6:99.
rows.anchor: وهم الذين آمنوا بالله وحده ، كما قال تعالى : { إن في ذلكم لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse recalls the creation of humanity's vast population from one familiar origin; its creator alone deserves worship, and human creation is among the greatest signs.
rows.anchor: هذا تذكير بخلق الإنسان وكيف نشأ هذا العدد العظيم من نفس واحدة كما هو معلوم لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Defining subject and predicate makes the claim restrictive, reproaching polytheists for worshipping others alongside their creator, as in the preceding verse's argument.
rows.anchor: والقصر الحاصل من تعريف المسند إليه والمسند تعريض بالمشركين ، إذ أشركوا في عبادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Insha means originating or bringing into existence; the pronoun refers to all humanity, and the single soul is Adam.
rows.anchor: والإنشاء : الإحداث والإيجاد . والضمير المنصوب مراد به البشر كلهم . والنفس الواحدة هي آدم
